thread.title: CIA Director John Ratcliffe Warns Russia Against Attacking NATO During Moscow Trip
thread.title_full: CIA Director John Ratcliffe Warns Russia Against Attacking NATO During Moscow Trip

author: Ahmed Ibrahim World Editor
title: CIA Director John Ratcliffe Warns Russia Against Attacking NATO During Moscow Trip
text:
Central Intelligence Agency Director John Ratcliffe traveled to Moscow for an unannounced visit aimed at warning Russia against launching any attacks on member states of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, according to people familiar with the matter. The secretive trip, which took place on Tuesday, marked Ratcliffe’s first known visit to Russia as CIA director. The visit came to light after a U.S. Air Force jet was spotted arriving at a Moscow airport and a diplomatic motorcade traveled through the Russian capital.
CIA Director John Ratcliffe Warns Russia Against Attacking NATO During Moscow Trip
U.S. intelligence assessments have recently indicated that Russian President Vladimir Putin could be willing to authorize provocative actions on NATO territory. These operations could include cyberattacks, hybrid actions, and a limited assault or small-scale land incursion—potentially targeting a Baltic nation—that fall short of conventional military action. According to U.S. officials, the likely goal would be to test NATO’s unity and the willingness of the administration of U.S. President Donald Trump to defend alliance allies. Officials noted that a pattern of recent Russian actions has sparked concerns, including drone incursions into Romania, a Russian missile crossing into Poland, and an uptick in alleged sabotage and cyberattacks across Europe.
Ukraine was informed in advance of the U.S. delegation’s travel to Moscow and was asked to hold off on military strikes for the duration of the visit, a senior Ukrainian official stated. During the discussions, Ratcliffe also addressed the conflict involving Iran, warning of additional sanctions if the Strait of Hormuz does not reopen to shipping traffic.
The Kremlin Response and Previous Precedents
The Kremlin confirmed that Ratcliffe engaged in talks with Russian intelligence officials during his time in Moscow, though he did not hold a meeting with Putin. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters that Putin was kept informed of the outcome without delay, declining to provide specific details on the topics discussed beyond confirming contacts through the security services. Peskov noted that while intelligence contacts continue during difficult periods in bilateral relations, it remains too early to determine whether the dialogue will help steer relations out of their profound crisis.
The last known visit to the Russian capital by a CIA director occurred in November 2021, when Ratcliffe’s predecessor, William Burns, met with Putin months before the war in Ukraine began. Ratcliffe stands as one of the highest-ranking U.S. officials to visit Russia since the war started in 2022.
President Trump Downplays the Purpose of the Visit
President Trump confirmed the overseas travel in an interview on the Glenn Beck Program, describing the journey as semi-routine
and downplaying its connection to NATO testing or Iran sanctions. When asked directly whether Ratcliffe traveled to discuss potential Russian actions against NATO or to address Iran, Trump replied, None of the above.
Instead, Trump suggested the trip was tied to broader diplomatic efforts to end the ongoing war in Ukraine. Now something may come out of it. We’re working very hard to get that war ended,
Trump stated during the interview, adding that Ratcliffe was not in Moscow for the speculative reasons raised by interviewers. The White House did not respond to multiple Agence France-Presse requests for comment, and the CIA declined to comment on the reasons behind the trip.

The visit came to light after a U.S. Air Force jet was spotted arriving at a Moscow airport and a diplomatic motorcade traveled through the Russian capital. Ukraine was informed in advance of the U.S. delegation’s travel to Moscow and was asked to hold off on military strikes for the duration of the visit, a senior Ukrainian official stated.
